answer:
RESULT — bix-43-q5. DE is complete and validated; the Reactome_2022 enrichment could NOT be computed as specified (Amendment 3 exhausted → option C+substitute), so the mechanism call below is computed on a labelled hand-curated marker panel plus knowledge-free co-expression evidence, not on Reactome.

ANSWER (concise, with the deviation flagged): The CBD/cisplatin combination signature is an anti-proliferative, DNA-damage-driven arrest response: TP53-target induction (CDKN1A, MDM2-type programme; FDXR, BTG2, ZMAT3, TP53INP1, AEN, PHLDA3, TNFRSF10C, FAS, BAX) together with coordinated repression of the mitotic G2/M + E2F/G1-S proliferation programme and shutdown of the HIF-target glycolytic programme (GPI, ALDOA/ALDOC, ENO1/2, PGK1, LDHA, PFKFB3/4, ANKRD37, HILPDA, ANGPTL4, BNIP3, PLOD2, VEGFA) and of SREBP cholesterol biosynthesis; the CBD-specific AhR/xenobiotic axis (CYP1A1 +5.0x, AHRR +5.6x, CYP1B1, TIPARP, NQO1, ALDH1A3) is the third coherent programme. Primary enriched mechanism = cell-cycle arrest / DNA-damage (p53) response with glycolytic-metabolic shutdown — not an inflammatory, interferon, NF-kB or ribosome/translation response (all non-significant). Because gseapy/Reactome_2022 was unavailable offline, I do NOT report a verbatim Reactome term as if it had been computed; in Reactome_2022 vocabulary the candidate terms are the "Cell Cycle / Cell Cycle Checkpoints / TP53 Regulates Transcription of Cell Cycle Genes" family (down), "Regulation of glycolysis by glycolytic enzymes / Glycolysis" (down) and, on small-term enrichment, "Aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalling / Nuclear Receptor transcription pathway" (up).

1) INPUTS (read-only pass, as requested)
• counts_raw_unfiltered.csv: 63,677 × 30; int64 raw counts (all exactly integer, min 0, max 906,308), no NA/missing, 0 duplicate and 0 non-ENSG row IDs; 27,954 all-zero rows; columns <group>_<replicate> 1_1…10_3 (10 groups × 3).
• sample_layout.csv: 10 groups × 3 reps; SampleID "g-r" ↔ column "g_r". 1 Untreated (control) | 2 Serum_starvation | 3 DMSO (vehicle) | 4 DMSO_Serum_starvation | 5 Cisplatin_IC50 (cisplatin alone) | 6 Cisplatin_IC50_Serum_starvation_16h | 7 CBD_IC50 (CBD alone) | 8 CBD_IC50_Serum_starvation_16h | 9 Cisplatin_IC50_CBD_IC50 (COMBINATION) | 10 Cisplatin_IC50_CBD_IC50_Serum_starvation_16h (combo in starved format). Group labels alone cannot tell whether the question means 9 or 10, nor whether control = Untreated vs DMSO — handled by the sensitivity grid, not guessed.
• ensg_to_gene_name.tsv: 86,369 unique ENSG, 0 duplicate keys, 0 NA symbols; covers 53,636/63,677 rows = 84.23%; 7,247 symbols shared by >1 ENSG in the file (only 9 such symbols among the tested genes, e.g. Y_RNA).

2) DE (Amendments 1,2,4) — analysis/bix43_q5_final.py + deseq_engine.py (no R/pydeseq2 offline)
Engine: median-of-ratios SF → NB2 GLM, design ~Group, all 30 samples → gene-wise dispersion by df-corrected method of moments (DESeq2 geneEstimator="moment") → parametric trend a0+a1/x → shrinkage mean(gene-wise,trend) → Wald contrast on the fixed-dispersion refit; baseMean = mean normalised count. Pre-filter ≥5 counts in ≥3 samples = 22,089 genes; baseMean>10 = 16,513 (unchanged by the pre-filter).
Two documented engine bugs were found and fixed by validation, both material: (i) profile-MLE dispersion was downward-biased (median d/truth 0.59) → null p<0.05 rate 14%; the moment estimator fixed it; (ii) min-normalised-count trend fit exploded (trend→1e4 for 5,194 genes) → trend now fit on baseMean.
Validation (10×3 sim, 100 planted DE): SF log-corr 0.9998; null contrasts p<0.05 = 0.062/0.064/0.056; power(raw p)=0.907 (empirical FDR of the raw-p rule 0.567 — i.e. the briefed rule is permissive by construction); power(padj)=0.814, FDR(padj)=0.122; median |log2FC| error 0.29; Jaccard shrunken-vs-unshrunken NB GLM 0.757. Label-permutation on the real counts: frac p<0.05 = 0.024/0.079/0.023.

3) DE lists (denominator 16,513 baseMean>10) — PRIMARY threshold raw p<0.05 & |LFC|>0.5 & baseMean>10
| contrast | threshold | n_DE | up | down | unmapped dropped | dup collapsed | symbols fed to enrichment |
| 9 Cis+CBD vs 1 Untreated (PRIMARY) | raw p | 2,031 (12.3%) | 1,112 | 919 | 132 | 0 | 1,899 |
| 9 vs 1 | padj | 1,698 | 941 | 757 | 97 | 0 | 1,601 |
| 9 vs 3 DMSO | raw p | 1,722 | 944 | 778 | 103 | 1 | 1,618 |
| 9 vs 3 | padj | 1,321 | 753 | 568 | 65 | 0 | 1,256 |
| 10 vs 4 | raw p | 2,645 | 1,421 | 1,224 | 135 | 0 | 2,510 |
| 10 vs 4 | padj | 2,334 | 1,265 | 1,069 | 100 | 0 | 2,234 |
| 10 vs 2 | raw p | 2,568 | 1,321 | 1,247 | 135 | 1 | 2,432 |
| 10 vs 2 | padj | 2,268 | 1,173 | 1,095 | 108 | 0 | 2,160 |
vs-single-agents/interaction = synergy question, omitted per agreement (only used descriptively in §4).

4) Enrichment — COMPUTED on a labelled SUBSTITUTE
Provisioning exhausted and reported: pip install gseapy → "Temporary failure in name resolution" (4 retries, no index/mirror configured; pip config shows no pip.conf anywhere); no PROXY/PIP_* env vars; no conda/mamba/uv/R; pip cache empty; filesystem-wide search for *.gmt, *reactome*, *kegg*, *.obo, *pathway*, *geneset*, *.whl, other site-packages → zero hits; raw-IP sockets (151.101.0.223:443, 1.1.1.1:443, 8.8.8.8:53) → "Network is unreachable"; no /etc/resolv.conf, no other mounts with references. So: no gseapy, no network, no gene-set library of ANY kind.
Substitute: 15 hand-curated panels (membership printed in out/marker_panel_membership.txt), scored with the Enrichr-identical statistic (one-sided hypergeometric, background = 20,814 symbol-mapped testable genes, BH; 30 contrast×threshold×panel tests). PRIMARY (9 vs 1, raw-p list, 1,899 symbols):
1 Hypoxia/glycolysis (HIF-target) 23/31, exp 2.8, P 4.1e-18, q 6.2e-17, 29 down/2 up, median LFC −0.77
2 p53/DNA-damage (TP53 targets) 18/37, exp 3.4, P 5.8e-10, q 4.3e-09, 30 up/6 down, median LFC +0.45
3 AhR/xenobiotic 8/13, exp 1.2, P 4.0e-06, q 2.0e-05, 10 up/2 down, median LFC +0.69
4 Circadian clock 7/11, q 4.6e-05 (mixed) 5 EMT/adhesion/TGF-β 8/24, q 2.7e-03 (mixed) 6 ATF4/ISR 6/18, q 1.0e-02 (mixed)
Non-enriched: interferon/antiviral (q 0.93), NF-kB/inflammation (0.82), autophagy/lysosome (0.87), ribosome/translation (1.0), OXPHOS (1.0). The top terms collapse into ONE theme — proliferation/metabolic arrest (p53-on, cell-cycle-off, glycolysis-off) — not several directions. Rank-based tests add mitotic G2/M (1.3e-10, 29/29 down), E2F/G1-S (2.9e-05), cholesterol/SREBP (1.1e-05, 25/26 down) as coordinately shifted below the |LFC| cut.
Control/threshold invariance: glycolysis-down + p53-up are the top two for BOTH 9v1 and 9v3 under BOTH raw p and padj; for 10v4 and 10v2 the top panels are mitotic G2/M down (28/29, q 2.4e-25) and cholesterol/SREBP down (q 1.2e-15) with p53 up still in the top three. So the DNA-damage/p53 + cell-cycle-down axis is control-invariant; the metabolic (glycolysis) component is strongest against the non-starved controls.
Knowledge-free support (no panel): average-linkage clustering of DE genes on group-mean profiles (r≥0.75) → 161 modules; largest 232 genes (median LFC −0.78) and 2nd 149 genes (−0.68) are glycolysis/hypoxia/ATF4 genes; largest up-module 125 genes (+0.71) contains TIPARP, THBS1, NR4A3, CCN1/CCN2, TFRC.
Per-arm descriptives (mean panel LFC vs Untreated; NOT an interaction test): p53 targets cisplatin +0.62 / CBD −0.15 / combo +0.59; AhR targets cisplatin +0.27 / CBD +0.95 / combo +0.99; mitotic genes cisplatin −0.04 / CBD +0.09 / combo −0.42 (combo+SS −0.78).

5) ARTIFACT (all executed, log in analysis/out/run_log.txt)
analysis/bix43_q5_final.py = executed pipeline; deseq_engine.py; marker_panel.py (substitute panel); validate.py; run_enrichment_gseapy.py (ready-to-run gseapy.enrichr(gene_sets="Reactome_2022") on the 1,899-symbol pooled list + up/down); out/results_full_{9_vs_1,9_vs_3,10_vs_4,10_vs_2}.csv (full annotated DE tables); out/DE_primary_rawp.csv + DE_primary_padj.csv; out/symbols_primary_*.{txt}; out/enrichment_results_all_contrasts.csv; out/coex_modules.csv; out/summary.json; REPORT.md.

LIMITATIONS: (1) the actual Reactome_2022/gseapy result is absent — the mechanism statement is computed from a hand-curated panel plus co-expression evidence, and panel membership is my own curation, so it cannot be quoted as a Reactome term or an Enrichr P-value; (2) DE is my DESeq2-equivalent port, not R DESeq2 — calibrated at n=3 but mildly anti-conservative (null 6%), and no COOK's-distance outlier filtering was implemented, so extreme p-values (e.g. GDA p≈1e-133, from genuinely tight replicates: within-group CV 3–5%) may be over-stated; (3) "combination" = group 9 as primary; group 10 shifts the emphasis to cell-cycle/cholesterol; (4) raw-p thresholding is permissive by design (empirical FDR ~0.57 in simulation) — padj lists give the same top terms; (5) enrichment ran on 1,899/2,031 DE genes (132 unmapped ENSG dropped, 0 duplicate symbols collapsed); (6) panel sizes are small (11–37 genes), so substitute P-values are not comparable to Enrichr library-scale terms.

payload.answer: Anti-proliferative DNA-damage / cell-cycle-arrest mechanism: the CBD/cisplatin combination (Cisplatin_IC50_CBD_IC50 vs Untreated) induces the p53/DNA-damage transcriptional programme and AhR/xenobiotic metabolism (CYP1A1, AHRR, CYP1B1, TIPARP) while coordinately repressing the mitotic G2/M + E2F/G1-S cell-cycle programme, the HIF-target glycolytic programme and SREBP cholesterol biosynthesis; i.e. the primary enriched mechanism is cell-cycle arrest / p53-mediated DNA-damage response with glycolytic-metabolic shutdown, not inflammation/interferon/NF-kB. NOTE: gseapy + Reactome_2022 could not be executed in this offline sandbox (no network, no gene-set library on disk), so the Reactome term string was not computed; this mechanism call is computed on a clearly labelled hand-curated marker panel (Enrichr-identical hypergeometric + BH) plus knowledge-free co-expression modules, with the ready-to-run gseapy.enrichr(gene_sets='Reactome_2022') script supplied for the final verbatim term.
payload.enrichment_engine_used: local Enrichr-equivalent hypergeometric on hand-curated marker panel (substitute for gseapy/Reactome_2022)
